earlier_scan.source_named: Menick, Raymond 1995. Moi, a language of the West Papuan phylum: A preview. In Tales from a concave world, Leiden, 55-73 (phonology cited on Wikipedia; no online full text found).

new_statements.citation: one of the works listed for this language (see the verification note)
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Both listed works were marked silent and both were re-opened (above); as a further spot-check of a silent work in the folder, Stokhof & Flassy 1985 (pp. 66 and 121-122 = pp. 62, 117-118): p. 62 note 3 'underlined syllables are stressed: tolom I sit' (Kamma's 1934 list); §4.2 pp. 117-118 sorts Kamma's Mooi forms into '1. M forms without stress indication', '2. M forms with stress: V V́' (suwòl 'eye', kesá 'armpit', kubús 'tendon', dalá 'male', suwòn 'main post', malá 'hill', sená 'moon', kemá 'proa', malán 'light': second syllable) and '3. M forms with stress: V́ V' (first syllable). This is raw data from Kamma's marks with both positions attested, framed as a Mooi-Tehit correspondence set;…

sources.citation: Gifelem, Agustinus Gidion & La Ode Madina. 2021. Pola persukuan bahasa Moi ragam Kelin di Kampung Kalayili, Distrik Kalayili, Kabupaten Sorong. KREDO: Jurnal Ilmiah Bahasa dan Sastra 5(1). DOI 10.24176/kredo.v5i1.6131
sources.note: Syllable-pattern study of the Kelin variety (patterns V, VK, KV, KVK, VKV, VKK, KKV, KVV); no occurrence of 'tekanan', 'aksen' or stress anywhere in the text.

sources.citation: Grambank, language page moii1235 (coder H. Hammarström; sources Menick 1995, 1996, 2000)
sources.note: No prosodic features coded; confirms the only descriptive sources used are the three Menick items.

sources.citation: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry. 1987. A survey of some West Papuan phylum languages. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 4: 25-80. Jayapura: SIL / Universitas Cenderawasih.
sources.note: Section 3.3 'Phonological features' (pp. 30-32) compares tone, syllable count, nasalised vowels, prenasalised stops and vowel harmony: Moi has no tone (Table 2, p. 32: 'Moi x 2 syllables x x y'), 65% of Moi words are disyllabic, regressive vowel harmony in prefixes. Stress is never mentioned.
sources.venue: Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures

sources.citation: OLAC record for mxn (the Internet Archive 2026-01-14) and Cocoon/CNRS-LACITO deposit by Daniel Krauße (2024-2025; sponsors ANR, CNRS, BRIN), e.g. 'Lexicon: Minimal pairs stab, sick, etc.' DOI 10.60714/cocoon.09f3396e-cac1-4f02-b339-6ecac18f02a9
sources.note: Recent documentation corpus (recordings of minimal pairs, lexicon, demonstratives, texts; also Voorhoeve's 1982 PARADISEC tapes CLV1-062/063/065/087/255/256). No written phonology or stress description is listed; the OLAC 'language descriptions' entries are only Glottolog and the Rosetta extract of Menick 2000.

sources.citation: Krauße, Daniel. 2024-. Moi language documentation (Cocoon / CNRS-LACITO deposit; ANR-CNRS-BRIN project), including 'Lexicon: Minimal pairs' recordings with Willem Hendrik Osok, Demas Magablo, Toryanus Kalami; any grammar or phonology write-up arising from it.
sources.note: The only current fieldwork on Moi; minimal-pair elicitation implies phonological analysis, and a sketch or phonology paper may exist or be forthcoming. Recordings are open; no written description located.

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Marian Klamer. 2018. The Papuan languages of East Nusantara and the Bird's Head. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Areal overview with a phonology section that may summarise word prosody of West Bird's Head languages (would at best be second-hand from Menick 1995).
sources.venue: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area

sources.citation: Menick, Raymond H. 2000. Moi. In Ger P. Reesink (ed.), Studies in Irian Languages Part II (NUSA 47), 7-24. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Indonesia Atma Jaya.
sources.note: One-page sketch (p. 7) plus a glossed text. Phonology limited to: 'Moi has fourteen phonemic consonants.. There are fourteen vowel phonemes in Moi: five short and five long vowels.. and four diphthongs'. Nothing on stress, accent or tone; p. 8: 'A more detailed description is still in preparation.'
sources.venue: Studies in Irian Languages Part II (NUSA 47)

sources.citation: Menick, Raymond H. 1996. Verb sequences in Moi. In Ger P. Reesink (ed.), Studies in Irian Languages Part I (NUSA 40), 41-60. Jakarta: Atma Jaya.
sources.note: Syntax paper (serial verbs); no phonology, no mention of stress.
sources.venue: Studies in Irian Languages Part I (NUSA 40)

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Moi language' (en), phonology section, citing Menick 1995 pp. 55-73
sources.note: Gives consonant and vowel tables attributed to Menick 1995 (and notes free variation of [ʔ]/k finally, /i,u/ as [ɪ,ʊ]); says nothing about stress, tone or syllable structure.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. & Don A.L. Flassy. 1985. A recently discovered M(o)oi vocabulary in the National Museum (Jakarta). In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 22 (Pacific Linguistics A-63), 53-130. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A63.53
sources.note: Section 3.2 'Mooi data' (p. 62, PDF 66) only explains Kamma's 1934 notation: '3. underlined syllables are stressed: tolom I sit.'; section 4.2 (p. 117-118) sorts Kamma's forms into 'M forms without stress indication' and 'M forms with stress' but states no placement rule. The line 'The place of the stress is distinctive and is indicated by [ ' ]' (p. 64, PDF 68) belongs to the TEHIT commentary (3.3), not to Moi.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 22 (Pacific Linguistics A-63)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x page moii1235 and reference pages 313179 / Grambank source pages
sources.note: Six descriptive references (the ones above plus two UNIPA Manokwari MA theses on pronouns and affixation); no phonology/stress source beyond Ansani & Fautngil 1983 and Menick 1995.
'mxn Moi' occurs only in the ISO language table; no lect, pattern or source record for Moi, i.e. StressTyp2 has no stress data for it.

sources.citation: Gifelem, Agustinus G. & Frenny S. Pormes. 2019. Fonem bahasa Moi ragam Kelin di Distrik Klaili Kabupaten Sorong. Akrab Juara: Jurnal Ilmu-ilmu Sosial 4(3) (Agustus 2019): 99-115. tone.quote: Sebagaimana dikemukakan di atas bahwa fonem konsonan bahasa Moi Ragam Moi Kelin berjumlah empat belas fonem dan lima fonem vokal. Keempat belas fonem konsonan dan lima vocal tersebut masing-masing antara lain Fonem konsonan, /b/,/d/,/f/,/g/,/k/,/l/,/m/, /n/,/p/,/r/,/s/,/t/,/w/,/y/, dan Fonem vocal, /a/, /e/,/i/,/o/,/u/
tone.locator: p. 114, section 4.2.2 (end of consonant list) / 4.2.3 'Variasi Bunyi Bahasa Moi'
tone.translation: As stated above, the consonant phonemes of the Moi language, Moi Kelin variety, number fourteen phonemes and five vowel phonemes. The fourteen consonant phonemes and five vowels are, respectively, consonant phonemes /b d f g k l m n p r s t w y/ and vowel phonemes /a e i o u/. (Inventory statement only; the article has no tone or stress passage.)
